From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call follow-up: Nimble AI perf evaluation & lab proposal

Hi Kyle — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap of call (TL;DR)
- You run a semi-real-time generation pipeline for customer support summaries (avg prompt ~420 tokens, bursts to 2k tokens).
- Top concerns: p95/p99 latency under load, sustainable tokens/sec when batched, and deterministic fallbacks across regions.
- You ran RedTeam & Hyperscaler PoCs last quarter; want a head-to-head that mirrors peak traffic for SLA gating.

Proposed lab (short):
1) A/B: Redwood Dedicated (quant + KV caching) vs Hyperscaler managed endpoint (your existing provider)
2) Workload: 3 traffic profiles — baseline (steady), midday-burst (3x), and microburst (many short requests).
3) Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, median tokens/sec, tail KS for latency, token cost per million, memory/KV hit-rate.
4) Test inputs: use your anonymized sample payload set (you mentioned ~2k requests) — attach a tokenized sample here if helpful.
5) Timeline: 2-week lab window, 3 days to onboard + run 4 test permutations (we can parallelize).

Ask from you: share the anonymized sample payloads and any hard SLOs (p95 target, cost ceiling). I attached a lightweight lab spec (redwood_lab_spec_v1.md) and a sample payload stub so we align on posture.

Notes on differentiators to highlight in lab:
- Redwood autoscaling + prewarming for steady p95 targets (reduces cold-start tail you saw).
- Prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated context tokens and improve tokens/sec for multi-turn flows.
- Quantization profiles we can toggle to trade cost vs latency; we'll capture quality metrics so you can compare MRR/customer-facing impact.

Next steps (proposal):
- If you can share payloads and confirm the three traffic profiles by Monday 11/8, Dev and Marissa will draft the exact runbook and assign test windows.
- We can provision a Dedicated trial pool for the lab (no billing until you sign off on post-lab changes).

Thanks again — happy to hop on another 30m if you want to walk through the lab spec.

Best,

Eve / Dev — attaching draft runbook and measurement checklist (redwood_lab_spec_v1.md attached). Highlights and proposed defaults below: 

Runbook highlights:
- Test window: 11/15–11/19 (reserve 4 full test days, 1 warmup day).
- Traffic profiles:
  * Baseline: 200 rps steady, 420-token avg, 95% single-turn
  * Midday-burst: 600 rps sustained 30m windows (3x baseline), same payload mix
  * Microburst: 1k concurrent short requests for 2m bursts (simulate spikes)
- Measurement bins:
  * p50/p95/p99 measured from server-side request completion timestamps; report both request-level latency and server-CPU/GPU-side latency.
  * Tokens/sec: compute both per-instance (tokens generated / active-gen-time) and cluster aggregate (tokens generated / wall-clock). Report 10s, 1m moving averages.
- KV and cache metrics: KV hit-rate, average KV retrieval latency, cache eviction rates.
- Quality checks: sample 1% of outputs for rouge/semantic similarity vs baseline to ensure quant/opt doesn't regress.
- Cost accounting: tokens billed, infra hours, and estimated per-million-token cost for both Redwood Dedicated and Hyperscaler baseline.

Fallbacks & modes:
- We'll run Redwood Dedicated with quantization profile Q4_0 and then a Q8 comparison if we need to trade latency.
- If Dedicated hits cold-start tail, we'll show a fallback using Redwood Hosted with autoscale to demonstrate graceful degradation and cost delta.

Deliverables for kickoff (11/12):
- Final runbook (this draft)
- Access & credentials: nimble_sample_payloads.json (they will upload) + non-prod attestation (they provided)
- Measurement dashboard links (we will provision and share)

I can run the initial lab orchestration and capture metrics. Dev, please confirm the exact command-line for the load generator and whether you want to pin sequence length or use their tokenization verbatim.
